per_window.ps-ns: Free WT at 298 K in MES: rigid backbone (average S2 above 0.9, tau_c 13.81 ns) with local flexibility at Val80 (S2 0.57) and two loops (J4, J5; r2). Clavulanate adduct loses rigidity at the helix 2/7 interface (J10). K234R gains flexibility at Ile247 and G132N around Ser70 (J13, J16; r8).
per_window.us-ms: dynamic_in_window for free WT at 298 K in phosphate-free MES: two-field group fit of eight active-site amides gives kex (8.6 ± 0.6) x 10^2 s-1, pB and delta omega not determinable (J1; r1, r4 restates it). Four anion-site amides (Ser70, Ser130, Thr235, Thr237) stay broadened beyond detection in MES at pH 6.0 and 6.4 and after phosphate titration (J2; r18, r1, r7). K234R removes the dispersion (J12); G132N extends broadening (J15); avibactam adduct speeds exchange to about 3,400 s-1 (J7); clavulanate adduct keeps it with more broadening (J8). Double mutants in phosphate show no dispersion (J21, J22).
per_window.slower_than_ms: no_evidence_in_window for free WT: CEST at 298 and 288 K finds nothing in 20-200 s-1 (J3; r2). G132N exchanges at 88 ± 6 s-1 with pB 40% (J14; r6); directed-evolution mutants show peak doubling (J19); clavulanate-adduct doubling is unresolved (J9). Free and clavulanate-bound WT do not interconvert on the chemical-shift timescale (r18; 0.3 mM BlaC with 1.5 mM clavulanate in 100 mM MES or sodium phosphate, pH 6.4, 298 K), a covalent-chemistry rate, not conformational exchange.
per_window.undetermined: MD of WT (5 x 1 us) shows an active site dominated by state A and 604 ns residence of the Phe68-Asn245 contact; states A' and B appear only in the D233A/D246A variants, with B more populated in D246A (J6, md_only). Sulbactam reaction times in crystals (10-90 ms) are ligand reaction, not exchange (J11, unresolved). Mutant crystal structures show alternate conformations or disorder (G132N J17, directed evolution J20, I105R J24); the I105Y-S130G alternates are suspected crystal or pH 4.5 artefacts (J23). Pro107 variants show fast closed/open exchange coupled to dimerisation (J25).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes: at 298 K in 94 mM MES pH 6.4 without phosphate, free wild-type BlaC exchanges on the low-millisecond scale around the active site, with a two-field group fit of eight amides giving kex (8.6 ± 0.6) x 10^2 s-1 and no determinable population or shift difference; the four anion-site amides Ser70, Ser130, Thr235 and Thr237 (entry 43, 101, 210, 212) are broadened beyond detection, which the authors calculate would require, if it were the same 860 s-1 process, a minor state above 15% with a shift difference above 0.1 ppm (1H) and/or 1 ppm (15N); CEST at 288 and 298 K finds no slower exchange in the 20-200 s-1 range.
open_conflicts: Origin of the four missing anion-site amides: Elings 2020 links them to the 860 s-1 process via a Bloch-McConnell estimate (pB above 15% with delta omega above 0.1 ppm 1H and/or 1 ppm 15N), while the same paper cannot determine pB from dispersion and Elings 2021 says only that 'another process' than phosphate exchange is responsible (J1 vs J2); one process or two is unresolved.

Functional role: Elings 2020 suggests the 860 s-1 exchange may matter for catalysis because it exceeds kcat 111 s-1; Elings 2021 finds no dispersion in the active K234R mutant and concludes millisecond dynamics are not required (J1 vs J12).

Open versus closed apo state: a cached SAXS study of free BlaC (Sagar 2017, sources_cache/BLAC_CPMG/PMC5524718.txt) proposes an open apo shape, while Elings 2020 finds tau_c matching the closed crystal structure and no evidence for an open state (J5); the SAXS study has no evidence row, so the conflict is recorded but not judged.
Crystal alternates versus solution: G132N crystal double conformations match NMR state populations (J17 vs J14), but I105Y-S130G crystal double conformations have no NMR counterpart (J23 vs J21).
questions_for_gina: Which data set produced the RelaxDB BLAC_CPMG labels ('Rex > 2 Hz from 850 Hz data')? Elings 2020 free-state relaxation data are BMRB 27888 (94 mM MES pH 6.4, 298 K), but the papers use Rex thresholds of 3 s-1 (2020) and 5 s-1 (2021), and the four anion-site amides cannot carry labels; is 27888 the source?

The wild-type NMR evidence is all in MES (20 mM pH 6.0 in 2017; 94 mM pH 6.4 in 2020/2021), while every 2024-2025 mutant study used 100 mM phosphate, which binds the active site (KD 27 ± 11 mM). Should mutant-versus-WT dispersion comparisons across these buffers be treated as not comparable, and is MES itself (a sulfonate anion) a concern for the anion-site broadening?
protein_summary.buffer_note: Key apo WT NMR samples are phosphate-free: 20 mM MES pH 6.0 with 1 mM DTT (Elings 2017, r18) and 94 mM sodium MES pH 6.4 (Elings 2020/2021, r1-r8). Phosphate binds the active site specifically (KD 27 ± 11 mM; NaCl control showed no comparable shifts, r18), but titrating it neither restores nor explains the four missing anion-site amides (off-rate above 2 x 10^4 s-1, r7). Untested condition: no study compares MES with another non-anionic buffer, so an MES-sulfonate contribution at the anion site is neither shown nor excluded. All 2024-2025 mutant NMR (r10, r12, r16, r19; directed-evolution assignments were transferred from the 2017 WT data, BMRB 27067) used 100 mM sodium phosphate pH 6.4-6.5 with the active site occupied by phosphate, so their dispersion results are not like-for-like with the WT MES data. Crystal data used phosphate (G132N, sulbactam at pH 4.1) or acetate/zinc at pH 4.5 (I105Y-S130G). Anion-site context: Elings 2020 notes that in every published BlaC crystal structure the side chains of the four invisible residues (Ser70, Ser130, Thr235, Thr237) hydrogen-bond either a ligand carboxylate or a buffer phosphate or acetate ion, and Elings 2017 reports that 29 published structures have this site occupied by phosphate or a ligand carboxylate. Anions in a nominally inert buffer change behaviour: with 100 mM Na2SO4 added to MES, 50% recovery from clavulanate inhibition took 2.0 ± 0.5 h versus 13.8 ± 0.8 h in MES alone (100 uM BlaC, 1:5 clavulanate; Elings 2017 Table 3), and the authors state sulfate accelerates clavulanate hydrolysis, less than phosphate.

detection.method: 15N CPMG relaxation dispersion; 1H-15N TROSY-HSQC inspection
detection.detection_window: 15N CPMG at 850 MHz and 25 °C in 100 mM phosphate (active-site ligand present); nuCPMG range not stated in the row; detects roughly 0.1-10 ms exchange with sizable 15N shifts; authors allow faster (ns) motion. Slow regime: some possible peak splitting in TROSY-HSQC, unclear whether unassigned amides or second states (Fig. S5a), left unresolved.

judgments.reason: The I105Y-S130G double mutant shows no significant relaxation dispersion at 25 °C in phosphate buffer, and possible split peaks in the slow regime remain unexplained.
